div.head: Ine 62
div.ab: CVI. Þonne mon bið tyhtlan betygen, ⁊ hine mon bedrifeð to ceape, nah þonne self nane wiht to gesellanne beforan ceape: þonne gæð oðer mon, seleð his ceap fore, swa he þonne geþingian mæge, on ða rædenne, þe he him ga to honda, oð ðæt he his ceap him geinnian mæge: þonne betyhð hine mon eft oþre siðe ⁊ bedrifð to ceape: gif hine forð nele forstandan se ðe him ær ceap foresealde, ⁊ he hine þonne forfehð, þolige þonne his ceapes se, ðe he him ær foresealde.

CVI. Ðonne mon bið tyhtlan betogen, ⁊ hine mon bedrifeð to ceace, nah þonne sylf nane wiht to gesyllanne beforan ceace: þonne gæð oþer mon, selð his ceap fore, swa he þonne geþingian mæge, on ða rǽdene, ðe he him ga to honda, oþ ðæt he his ceap geinnian mæge: ðonne betyhð hine mon eft oþre siþe ⁊ bedrifþ to ceace: gif hine forð nele forstandon se þe him ceap ær foresealde, ⁊ he hine þonne forfehð, þolige þonne his ceapes, ðe he him ær foresealde.

Be þam þe man to ceace fordræfe. Ðonne mon bið tyhtlan betogen, ⁊ hine mon bedrifeð to ceace, nah ðonne sylf nan wiht to syllanne beforan ceace: ðonne gæð oðer man, sylað his ceap fore, swa he ðonne geðingian mæge, on ða ræddene, ðe he him ga to hánda, oð þæt he his ceap him geinnian mǽge: ðonne betyhð hine mon eft oðre siðe ⁊ bedrifþ to ceace: gyf he hine nylle forstandan forð se ðe him ær ceap foresealde, ⁊ he him ðonne forfehð, ðolie ðonne his ceapes se, ðe he him ær foresealde.

Quando aliquis homo fuerit accusatus et ad captale pertrahitur (fauces coartatur) nec habet idem aliquid ad dandum ante certamen, et uadit alius et dat suum captale pro eo tali pacto, ut idem transeat ei in manum, donec captale suum possit illi intimare: si iterum accusetur alia uice et ad componendum pertrahatur, si ei nolit preesse, qui captale suum pro eo dedit antea et hoc anticipauerit, perdat captale suum quod ante pro eo dederat.

[Be þam þe man to ceace fordræfe.] Ðonne mon bið tyhtlan betygen, ⁊ hine mon bedrifeð to ceace, nah þonne self nane wiht to gesellanne beforan ceace: þonne gæð oðer mon, seleð his ceap fore, swa he þonne geþingian mæge, on ða rædenne, þe he him ga to honda, oð ðæt he his ceap him geinnian mæge: þonne betyhð hine mon eft oþre siðe ⁊ bedrifð to ceace: gif hine forð nele forstandan se ðe him ær ceap foresealde, ⁊ he hine þonne forfehð, þolige þonne his ceapes se, ðe he him ær foresealde.

{CVI} Þonne mon bið tyhtlan betygen, ⁊ hine mon bidrifeð to ceape, nah þonne self nane whit to gesellanne beforan ceape: Þonne gæð oðer mon seleð his ceap fore, swa he þonne geþingian mæge, on ða rædenne, þe him ga to honda, oððæt he his ceap him geinnian mæge. Þonne betyhð hine mon eft oþre siðe ⁊ bedrifð to ceape: Gif hine forð nele forstandan se ðe him ær ceap for sealde, ⁊ he hine þonne forfehð, þolige þonne his ceapes se ðe he him ær fore sealde.

Wenn jemand einer Strafsache angeschuldigt ist und zum Kessel[fange] gezwungen wird, aber selbst nichts vor dem Kessel herzugeben besitzt: [wenn] dann jemand anders kommt [und] sein Gut vorschiesst — je wie er dann [mit dem Kläger] abmachen kann — auf die Bedingung hin, dass ihm der [Schuldner] diene, bis dass derselbe ihm sein [vorgeschossenes] Gut einbringen könne: es wird aber jener [Schuldner] späterhin zum zweiten Male verklagt und zum Kesselfange gezwungen: wenn [nun] der, welcher ihm früher Vorschuss gegeben hatte, ferner nicht für ihn einstehen will, und ihn [den Schuldigen, der zweite Kläger] nun fasst, dann verliere [der Gläubiger] sein Gut, das er ihm früher vorgeschossen hatte.

If someone is accused in a criminal matter and is forced to [the ordeal of] the cauldron, but himself possesses nothing to give before the cauldron: [if] then someone else comes [and] advances his goods — however he can then settle [with the plaintiff] — on the condition that the [debtor] serve him until he can repay him his [advanced] goods: but that [debtor] is later accused a second time and forced to the cauldron-ordeal: if [now] the one who earlier gave him the advance will no longer stand surety for him, and [the second plaintiff] now seizes him [the guilty man], then let [the creditor] lose his goods which he had earlier advanced to him.

If anyone is accused, and trial by ordeal is being forced upon him, and he has nothing to pay with, in order to escape the ordeal; and if another man goes and, on whatsoever terms he may be able to arrange, gives his goods instead, on condition that he [the accused] surrenders himself into his surety’s hands, until he can restore to him the goods he has pledged; and then if he is accused a second time, and trial by ordeal is forced upon him, and he who had pledged goods for him will not continue to stand for him, and the accuser arrests him—he who had given [a pledge] for him shall lose his goods.

When a charge is brought against a man, and he is driven to the ordeal, and he himself possesses nothing to give, in order to avoid the ordeal; and another man comes forward and gives his goods instead, on what terms he can obtain, on condition that he becomes subject to him until he can restore his property to him; and then he is again a second time accused and driven to the ordeal; if he who before gave goods on his behalf will not support him further, and he [the accuser] takes him, he [the creditor] is to lose his goods, which before he paid on his behalf.

When someone is accused of an offense, and he is required to compensate in goods and he does not have property to give for such compensation: if another man goes and gives his property for him – in whichever way he may settle [with the accuser] – [let it be] on the condition that [the accused] goes into his hands [in servitude] until he can restore to him [the value of] his property. If he is later accused a second time and required to compensate in goods: if the person who earlier gave the property for him does not wish again to stand up for him, and [the second accuser] captures him, then the man who earlier stood surety for him forfeits his property.

Mit ceape meint E wohl ‘Zahlungspflicht’. Weder kann -k mit -p dialektisch variieren, noch auch solch Wort zusammenhängen mit cippus (‘Stock’, das kāk [‘Pranger’] nach Bed. und Etymologie verwandt [!] sei) und ‘Strafwerkzeug’ heissen. Q’s Vorlage muss an einigen Stellen ceace gehabt haben (da er einmal, wohl mit cease verwechselnd, certamen, einmal faux missverstand), anderwärts ceape, wofür er meist captale setzt, einmal aber ‘Busszahlung’ frei deutend einführt. Neuere seit Lambarde legten ceap den Sinn ‘Pfand’ (s. o. zu 37⁴) unter, vielleicht aus 49, 1, wo zufällig der ‘Sachwert, das Vieh’ gepfändet ist, oder aus der Stelle u. Erkl. 11

By ceape E probably means ‘liability to pay’. Neither can -k vary dialectally with -p, nor can such a word be connected with cippus (‘stocks’, supposedly related [!] in meaning and etymology to kāk [‘pillory’]) and mean ‘instrument of punishment’. Q’s exemplar must in some places have had ceace (since he once misunderstood it as certamen, probably confusing it with cease, and once as faux), and elsewhere ceape, for which he mostly puts captale, but once, interpreting freely, introduces ‘payment of compensation’. Modern scholars since Lambarde have attributed to ceap the meaning ‘pledge’ (see above on 37⁴), perhaps from 49, 1, where it happens to be the ‘chattel, the cattle’ that is distrained, or from the passage below note 11

bedrifan to (s. Wb 1) ‘durch Klage zwingen zum Leiden einer prozessualischen Folge’; vgl. Fries. driva bei Richthofen Wb. In ähnlichem Sinne wird zwar auch ‘schlagen’ übertragen, aber ‘in Stock schlagen’ rechtfertigt sich damit hierfür nicht

bedrifan to (see Wb 1) ‘to compel by an accusation to suffer a procedural consequence’; cf. Fris. driva in Richthofen Wb. ‘Strike’ is indeed also used figuratively in a similar sense, but that does not justify ‘put in the stocks’ here

entweder zeitlich, d. h. ‘vór Ordalbeginn’, oder örtlich, ‘angesichts des Kessels’, oder wahrscheinlicher ‘in Vertretung, anstatt des Ordals’; vgl. was Thorpe zitiert: Jesus fastet 40 Tage beforan manna synnum. Alle 3 Bedd. sind möglich auch für das andere Beweismittel, den Eid: s. u. 71²

either temporal, i.e. ‘before the start of the ordeal’, or local, ‘in the presence of the cauldron’, or, more probably, ‘as a substitute, in place of the ordeal’; cf. what Thorpe quotes: Jesus fasts 40 days beforan manna synnum. All 3 meanings are possible for the other means of proof too, the oath: see below 71²

B modernisiert. — Der als schuldig sich Fühlende und vom Gericht Verdächtigte wagt das Ordal nicht, bei dessen Missglücken er friedlos würde, und besitzt doch nichts, um Kläger und Richter zu befriedigen. Da braucht er anderswo Bürgschaft (s. d. Gl 6. 13 b) oder hier einen Gelddarleiher; s. Gl Darlehn 6. a

B modernises. — The man who feels himself guilty and is suspected by the court does not dare to undergo the ordeal, failure in which would make him an outlaw, and yet he possesses nothing with which to satisfy plaintiff and judge. He then needs surety (see that word in Gl 6. 13 b) elsewhere, or here a moneylender; see Gl Darlehn 6. a
‘Ersatz’ (Schmid 543) ist allein zu eng: auch Busse und Strafgeld müssen bezahlt sein
‘Restitution’ (Schmid 543) alone is too narrow: compensation and fine too must have been paid
Vgl. Wb: forebetan, -gesellan, -(ge)þingian, -wyrcean ‘büssen (geben begleichen, tun) stellvertretend für’. — Vgl.: de manu ab enco redimenda Lex Salica 53; Brunner II 407
Cf. Wb: forebetan, -gesellan, -(ge)þingian, -wyrcean ‘to pay compensation (give, settle, do) on behalf of’. — Cf.: de manu ab enco redimenda Lex Salica 53; Brunner II 407
Nach II As 21 darf der Ordalprüfling nur übers Ersatzgeld (also mit Kläger) begleichend verhandeln
According to II As 21 the man undergoing the ordeal may negotiate a settlement only about the restitution (that is, with the plaintiff)

B konfundiert öfter Dat. und Acc. des Personale in Mittelengl. Weise; s. Wb: he. Q missversteht hine als auf ceap bezüglich; zu seiner Übs. von forfon vgl. Wb: anticipatio. — Nicht notwendig ‘vor anderem Gerichtshofe’, wie Stephens Hist. of criminal law I 69 meint

B often confuses the dat. and acc. of the personal pronoun in Middle English fashion; see Wb: he. Q misunderstands hine as referring to ceap; on his translation of forfon cf. Wb: anticipatio. — Not necessarily ‘before another court’, as Stephens Hist. of criminal law I 69 thinks

‘Wenn Selbstverpfändeter jemandem etwas verbricht, zahle Pfandgläubiger Schaden oder liefere Verpfändeten aus unter Verlust seiner Pfandsumme’; Fränk. Capit. in L. Sal. mitt. a. 803 c. 8 = Hn 89, 3. Andere Parallelen Brunner II 443. 478

‘If a self-pledged man commits an offence against anyone, let the pledgee pay the damage or hand over the pledged man, forfeiting his pledge-money’; Frankish Capit. in L. Sal. mitt. a. 803 c. 8 = Hn 89, 3. Other parallels Brunner II 443. 478
